Born at Stundwiller, Bas-Rhin, 17 September 1828, son of François Staebell and Marie Anne Casper;
in the 1846 census he was 17, at home on the Dorfgasse, where his father was the village field warden.
Left for America in 1853, possibly on the Mary Annah from Le Havre, and farmed near Freeport,
Illinois, where in 1855 he married Margaretha Philipps of his own village.
In September 1863 they came to Black Hawk County, Iowa, with $600, three horses and a few cattle,
and took up 80 acres of wild land in Barclay Township, which he built up to 244 acres in section 4,
with a set of buildings the local history called neat and thrifty.
In June 1881 he started a creamery on the farm, selling cream at 11 cents a pound.
A devout Catholic, he gave Saint Francis Church a painted banner of its patron saint on Christmas Day 1882.
He cast his first presidential vote, in 1856, for James Buchanan.
He retired in 1898, when his son Michael married and took over the farm, and died in October 1912;
his funeral was a Solemn High Mass at Saint Francis, and he lies there in the family plot beside Margaret and their
daughter Rose, who died of tuberculosis at sixteen.
Born at Stundwiller, Bas-Rhin, Alsace, on 4 March 1831, daughter of Antoine Philipps and Marie Angélique Schmitt.
She came to America in 1853, at 22, and lived two years at Buffalo with her sister;
in 1855 she moved to Freeport, Illinois, and married Frank Staebell, of her own village,
at Saint Mary’s Church there. Their first four children were born on the farm near Freeport.
In 1863 they moved to Barclay Township, Black Hawk County, Iowa, where they were among the first members of Saint
Francis parish; the parish history remembers a kind, hospitable woman who always welcomed the priest when he came
out to Barclay to say Mass. Of their ten children, Mary married John Fritz at Saint Francis on 17 January 1882,
in a double wedding with her sister Caroline.
Margaret had fifty grandchildren. She died at Barclay on 5 September 1904, aged 73,
after a year’s illness, and is buried at Saint Francis.
